transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?
Well… since I stopped working, I guess I just can’t really slow down. I’m up and moving around all day, going from one little job to the next, like there’s still a crew waiting on me or something.
When you're moving around all day like this, how would you describe your mood—do you feel unusually upbeat, energetic, or irritable, or more like you're anxious and can't relax?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t say upbeat, exactly. Maybe just kind of keyed up. Hard to settle, I guess.
How has your sleep been lately—are you sleeping less than usual but still feeling rested and full of energy, or are you having trouble sleeping because your mind won't stop racing with worry?
I’m not sure, really. Sleep’s… okay, I guess. I haven’t noticed feeling especially rested or anything like that. My mind does run some, but I don’t know if I’d call it worry.
How long has this feeling of being unable to slow down and staying busy all day been going on—days, weeks, or longer?
Longer. It got to be a real problem after I retired from handyman work… about a year and a couple months ago.
Have you noticed any changes in your memory, concentration, or ability to think clearly during this time?

Yeah… mostly concentration, I guess. If I’m painting or trying to plan out a story, and I hear a truck outside or think about something in the garden, my mind just… goes there. Then I kind of lose where I was.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things—like your health, finances, or family—even when there's no clear reason to, and does that worry feel hard to control?
I don’t think so. I mean, I worry some like anyone does, but it’s not like I’m sitting there all day worrying about everything. At least… I haven’t noticed it that way.

Before you retired, did you notice similar trouble staying focused or feeling restless, like as a teenager or in your earlier working years, or is this pattern something new that started around the time you stopped working?

I guess it wasn’t totally new. Even in grade school, teachers would say I was bright but… scattered. Losing pencils, blurting out answers, needing reminders to finish my work before recess—that kind of thing.

Between grade school and your retirement about a year ago, did you continue to notice this kind of distractibility and restlessness during your working years, or was there a period where it wasn't really a problem for you?
I’m not really sure. I mean… I worked, so I must’ve managed well enough. I don’t remember a long stretch where it felt completely gone, but I can’t say exactly how much of a problem it was either.
